messages:
maria: Quick flag — reproduced a nasty scale-down oscillation on dedicated pools. short burst -> scale up -> shortly after, autoscaler nukes nodes and we miss follow-up requests. repro attached.
chetan: yikes. can you paste the repro steps?
maria: steps: run this load pattern against tenant T-42: 
```bash
for i in {1..3}; do hey -z 60s -c 80 -q 50 http://svc/endpoint; sleep 20; done
```
first two runs trigger scale-up, third run happens after scale-down finishes. hits >99th latency.
elena: which metric triggered the downscale? allocation utilization? pod idle time?
maria: allocator reported low token headroom + node idle for 90s, downscale window kicked in.
ops-bot: autoscaler: scaled down pool "dedicated-gpu-pool-7" by 2 nodes (reason: idle-window=90s, cost-threshold).
max: interesting — does the autoscaler consider recent allocation spikes or just current instant util?
chetan: current impl uses a sliding average of node utilization over window W and an idle threshold. if avg < X we evict. windows are tuned to minimize cost but apparently too aggressive for bursty patterns.
elena: tradeoff: longer window -> cost, shorter -> missed bursts. maybe add a "shrink-protection" mode for tenants with burstiness.
maria: wanted to prototype something simpler: protect nodes for a minimum lifetime after scale-up. i.e., when we add nodes, tag them protected for M seconds and ignore idle signal until that expires.
max: that helps for quick re-surge cases. but if M is large we pay for idle time unnecessarily. can we make M dynamic based on observed burst frequency?
chetan: idea: per-tenant burst score: compute P(repeat spike within T) and set protection ~E[inter-spike interval]. adaptive.
elena: more signals: inflight queue depth, request rate derivative, KV cache hit rate (warm caches mean higher chance of follow-up), and prewarm credits.
maria: also need graceful drain: when we do evict, we should keep node in "pre-drain" for D seconds to allow in-flight completion and to let admission route to hot nodes.
max: and differentiate user-visible SLO vs internal cost SLO. For latency-critical tenants, prefer headroom even if idle. For cheaper tenants, be aggressive.
chetan: implementation sketch: 
1) when scale-up -> mark newly provisioned nodes with protection TTL P (adaptive).
2) autoscaler reads both long-window avg and recent-derivative; only consider eviction if both low and no recent spike signal.
3) introduce a "soft-evict" phase: mark nodes draining but keep them available for small bursts for S seconds, tracked by inflight accounting.
4) credit pool: grant tenants burst credits that can consume ephemeral headroom without triggering scale-up/down.

code-snippet for soft-evict conditions:
```go
if node.ProtectedUntil.After(now) { skipEvict(node) }
if avgUtil < low && derivative < eps && !recentSpike { evict(node) } else { markSoftDrain(node) }
```

elena: what about prewarm cost? we have cases where cache warming is heavy; protecting nodes helps but caches get evicted in downscale. perhaps cache-aware eviction: prefer evicting cold nodes first.
maria: agree — use per-node cache-score metric. evict lowest score first.
max: operational concerns: we need observability — dashboards for protected nodes, reasons for eviction, and a simulator to run patterns against policy.
chetan: rollout strategy: default on pilot tenants with high latency sensitivity. add metrics, run canary for 2 weeks. we need alerts for "repeated resurge after eviction".
elena: edge cases: if cluster exhausted, protection could starve new tenants. need global fairness: protection consumes logical headroom but should be capped per-pool.
maria: propose: protection consumes soft-reservation tokens. if soft-reservations exceed poolBudget, we lower protection aggressiveness.
max: cost model: simulate monthly cost increase for several P values. show diminishing returns.
chetan: action items: 
- maria: open RFC PR with adaptive protection algorithm and eviction flow (by EOD).
- elena: add cache-score metric and cheap exporter (next week).
- max: set up simulation harness + dashboard (start Monday).
- ops-bot: add alert "resurge-after-evict" when a tenant experiences >2 scale-ups within 5m after scale-down.

maria: thanks — want to avoid another on-call page at 3am :grimacing:
chetan: agreed. if anyone wants to pair on the RFC ping me.
elena: tagging @product to discuss SLA weight config? they should control per-tenant latency priority.
max: cool. will follow up with cost sims.
ops-bot: autoscaler: noted action "resurge-after-evict" alert created.
maria: closing loop — will post RFC link when ready.
